grades.reason: Describes RISC-V G-stage guest physical address translation (hgatp, Sv39x4, etc.). It does not explain why a VMM must intercept privileged guest instructions in trap-and-emulate.

grades.quote: The operation of a VMM is similar to that of an operating system. Like an operating system, it uses scheduling to divide processing time and uses page mapping to divide memory.
grades.reason: Gives general background on a VMM acting like an OS that divides CPU time and memory and presents a machine-like interface. It never says why privileged instructions must be trapped, so it is only auxiliary.

grades.quote: Trapping_ `satp` _accesses and the SFENCE.VMA and SINVAL.VMA instructions provides the hooks necessary to lazily populate shadow page tables._
grades.reason: Explains several reasons for trapping privileged guest operations (satp/SFENCE.VMA, WFI, SRET) in RISC-V. These include populating shadow page tables, switching to another guest, and emulating the hypervisor extension. It is useful but specific to RISC-V mechanisms and does not give the general rationale.

grades.quote: a VMM can keep processes running in separate virtual machines isolated from one another, even in the face of a security breach in one or both virtual machines’ operating systems.
grades.reason: Mentions that a VMM keeps virtual machines isolated and has complete power over them. This is loosely related to why the monitor must control guests, but it says nothing about intercepting privileged instructions.
